items.title: Elevance Health sues over $516M Medicare star ratings loss - Modern Healthcare
items.reason: This reports a lawsuit by a major payer (Elevance/Anthem) involving Medicare Advantage sanctions and financial penalties directly related to star ratings, which is a core enforcement and litigation topic affecting payer operations and revenue.
items.summary: Elevance Health has filed a lawsuit over a $516 million loss related to Medicare star ratings, representing a significant regulatory enforcement action involving one of the nation's largest health insurers. The suit challenges CMS decisions regarding star rating determinations that resulted in substantial financial penalties to the payer. This litigation directly impacts Elevance's Medicare Advantage business and demonstrates ongoing disputes between major payers and CMS over rating methodologies and their financial consequences. Revenue-cycle teams should monitor this case as outcomes could affect payer reimbursement pressures and network sustainability strategies that flow to provider payments.

items.summary: Jefferson Health Plans has filed a lawsuit against federal authorities challenging a decline in its Medicare Advantage star ratings for 2027. The suit contests the CMS methodology or process that resulted in the rating reduction, which directly affects the payer's performance metrics and reimbursement under the Medicare Advantage program. Star rating changes trigger financial consequences and network perception impacts that ripple through provider contracting and claims processing. This litigation is significant for revenue-cycle teams because Medicare Advantage star-rating disputes can influence payer solvency, network stability, and the likelihood of payment challenges or network changes affecting provider reimbursement.
